video.title: 2026 NBA Draft Recap: 7 Rookies To Draft + Winners & Losers

summary: Josh Lloyd recaps the first round of the 2026 NBA draft from a fantasy redraft angle. No projections have been done yet because trades and free agency are still to come. He names seven rookies worth drafting: Cameron Boozer (clear first rookie off the board), AJ Dybantsa and Darryn Peterson (both around top 80 picks), then Caleb Wilson, Darius Acuff Jr., Hannes Steinbach and Mikel Brown Jr. as late-round flyers. He says rookies usually start badly and then improve, calls the rookie wall a myth, and warns that ESPN-style rankings put too many rookies too high. He lists veterans who lose value because of the draft: Moussa Diabaté, Nolan Traoré, Keyonte George, Kyshawn George and Santi Aldama. He liked the drafts of Charlotte, Philadelphia, the Lakers and Brooklyn, and criticized Dallas plus several picks by Milwaukee, Golden State, Memphis, Sacramento and Atlanta.

rules.text: Projections must balance across a whole roster. A player's value depends on teammates, usage and minutes, so a team change can move usage a lot (example: Michael Porter Jr. in Brooklyn vs Denver).
rules.quote: Player moves from one team to another, there's fewer players there. Michael Porter goes to the Nets, usage way up.

rules.text: Don't overrate rookies in redraft. At best a class gives one top 50 player and three top 100 players.
rules.quote: At best you'll get one top 50 guy and three top 100 players. At best. So just always be aware of that.

rules.text: Top rookies are usually bad early and then improve. If you draft one early, accept the slow start and don't drop him.
rules.quote: So if you're drafting him early, you're going to have to just cop it early.

rules.text: The rookie wall is a myth. Roughly 90% of rookies get better as the season goes on.
rules.quote: Rookie wall is a myth. Go back and look at nearly every rookie. 90% of them get better.

rules.text: Don't count on late-season shutdowns by tanking teams giving rookies big minutes in March. That may not happen much anymore.
rules.quote: "Well, in March, they'll sit guys down, and this guy will cook." I I don't know if that's going to happen that much.

rules.text: Uncertain rookies belong in the flyer zone, around picks 120 to 130 in a 12-team league, which is the end of the active roster or start of the bench.
rules.quote: We're talking about a 12-man league, you're picking around 120. So, the start of your bench,

rules.text: For rookie flyers, use Summer League and preseason. If a player is named a starter, push him higher. If nothing happens in the first two weeks, drop him and maybe pick him up later.
rules.quote: you draft him and then you'd see what happens the first two weeks and

rules.text: A big man with blocks, threes, rebounds and good field goal percentage is a fantasy cheat code.
rules.quote: Cuz he will have the the the cheat code. Blocks, threes, rebounds, um field goal percentage for a big man.

rules.text: Losing even two to three minutes a game limits a player's upside and lowers his draft value.
rules.quote: lose two to three minutes off what he does, and it drops him down. And then your upside becomes limited.

rules.text: College players who dominate while four or five years older than their competition are a red flag. NBA role players are usually college stars.
rules.quote: I'm with these players who start dominating when they're five, four years older than their competition in college always is a red flag

rules.text: Hot starts built on unsustainable numbers, like extreme rim finishing, tend to fade.
